extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset of 21,336 verifiable, interactive Python software engineering tasks from 3,468 GitHub repositories. Each task includes a real-world issue, solution and test patches, executable environment configuration, pinned dependencies, test outcomes, and automatically generated quality metadata. A benchmark subset contains 294 tasks from 169 repositories.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, and Boris Yangel; Nebius
extraction.inLanguage: English is required for problem statements in the benchmark subset; the initial dataset release contains Python programming tasks.
extraction.citeAs: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, and Boris Yangel. SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2505.20411v2, 4 November 2025.
extraction.isLiveDataset: The benchmark is continuously updated using an automated supply of fresh tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A four-stage pipeline collects preliminary tasks, automatically configures installation instructions, verifies installation and tests through execution, and assesses task quality. GitHub Archive events are downloaded and merged with locally cloned GitHub repositories and their full commit histories. Issues are linked to pull requests that mention resolving them. Approximately 450,000 issue-linked pull requests from more than 30,000 permissively licensed repositories with over 75% Python code were initially collected, filtered to approximately 153,400 candidates, and processed into 21,336 verified tasks. Nonstandard or custom repository licenses were manually reviewed for permissive terms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Git tags provide project versions for approximately 95% of task instances; remaining tasks lack a version obtained this way. Pull request head commits may be unavailable, for example because a branch was deleted after merging. Some otherwise valid tasks cannot be included because dependencies are obsolete or unavailable, installation requires more interactive troubleshooting, or tests are flaky.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public GitHub events from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories cloned with full commit histories. Collected information includes issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, creation dates, labels, pull request merge status, last commits, and discussions. The collection targets permissively licensed repositories where Python accounts for more than 75% of codebase lines.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Tasks without a version obtainable from git tags are assigned unique versions so that each uses its own environment. When a pull request head_commit is unavailable, patch generation falls back to merge_commit and records the choice in task metadata.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Pull request changes are separated into solution patches for non-test files and test patches for test files. Patches preferentially compare head_commit against base_commit to isolate pull request changes. Project versions are normalized to major.minor and tasks are grouped by version, using the most recent base_commit in each group for environment setup. Problem statements concatenate issue titles and bodies; hints contain issue comments preceding the solution pull request's first commit. Deleted test files are excluded from test directives.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Candidates must have resolved issues, pull requests merged into the main branch, no linkage to multiple issues, descriptions longer than 10 characters, test additions or modifications, non-test code changes, and changes affecting 1–15 files. Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct identifies installation-related files, generates up to three candidate installation recipes, and refines failed recipes using error logs. Environments are installed in isolated containers. Valid tasks require at least one test to fail before the solution and pass afterward, all initially failing tests to pass afterward, and initially passing tests to remain passing. Tests are repeated and instances failing any run are excluded. Exact dependency versions are frozen and recorded after successful setup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Original merged pull requests supply gold solution patches and test patches. Execution logs produce FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS test labels. A Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct model fine-tuned on more than 3,800 examples using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified predicts Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness independently from the issue description, canonical solution patch, and test patch. These machine-generated quality labels are included in each task's metadata.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The automated quality assessor uses a 75/25 training/validation split with 413 validation examples. Reported accuracy and weighted F1 are 81% and 0.82 for Task Complexity, 67% and 0.65 for Test Patch Correctness, and 79% and 0.76 for Issue Clarity. Class-specific precision and recall are provided in Appendix F. The authors acknowledge that automated labels contain errors and cannot fully reproduce nuanced human judgment; users may filter tasks using these labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 0 human quality labels for SWE-rebench tasks; quality assessment is fully automated.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified human annotations; automated test execution and log parsers generate test-outcome labels.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors maintain continuously updated benchmark evaluations and a public leaderboard using fresh tasks. Issue and pull request creation dates are tracked against model release dates, and potentially contaminated evaluations are marked on the leaderboard. Future plans include increasing dataset volume, improving filtering, collecting tasks beyond issue-linked pull requests, supporting additional programming languages, and evaluating more models. No fixed update schedule, release-version policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and standardized, decontaminated benchmark are intended to accelerate open-source research, improve evaluation reliability, and promote transparent and fair model comparisons. The authors note that advancing autonomous software engineering agents may increase overreliance on AI-generated code or enable misuse to introduce vulnerabilities. They propose openness and rigorous benchmarking as mitigating practices.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The initial release is exclusively Python. Automated filtering and environment setup rely on heuristics and LLM interpretations; installation prompts were validated on only 18 repositories. Automated quality labels are imperfect, and some tasks may be underspecified or unsolvable solely from the issue, potentially incorrectly penalizing agents and lowering success rates relative to manually curated benchmarks. Flaky tests, obsolete or unpinned dependencies, installation requiring interactive troubleshooting, and custom test outputs that generic parsers cannot interpret can exclude valid tasks. The benchmark subset restricts issue language to English and favors low-to-moderate complexity, small patches, and recent issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating LLM-based software engineering agents in executable repository environments, particularly reinforcement learning with automatic verification. Quality metadata supports filtering by issue clarity, test correctness, and difficulty. The benchmark supports standardized comparisons using a fixed ReAct-style scaffold and prompts; each model is evaluated five times, with mean resolution rate, standard error, and pass@5 reported. Benchmark tasks require clean test logs, no more than three solution-modified files, solution patches of at most 500 words, English problem statements of 16–1,000 words, issues created in 2025, assessed difficulty below 3, and at most 50 fail-to-pass tests.
